exposure: Gestational age at elective repeat cesarean delivery (36-40 weeks)
outcome: Prematurity-related complications (Apgar score, assisted ventilation, intensive care admission, surfactant use, antibiotic use, seizures)
cohort: 785,340 women undergoing elective repeat cesarean delivery between 36 and 40 weeks gestation
finding: While prematurity-related complications were increased in newborns delivered by elective repeat cesarean delivery before 39 weeks compared to 40 weeks, this difference was not significant for African-American newborns after 38 weeks.
